form.officialName: Motion to Seal Criminal Conviction for Engaging in Prostitution

strategy.rationale: The binary is now in hand and is technically ready for Tier 0, but the adopted Maine legal design records the form itself as legally stale. Presence removed the location blocker only.

officialSource.hashReconciliation: Matches the sha256 pinned as a packetGenerator formCandidate in src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/ME-maine.json and the 166,837-byte sourceInspection in the committed field-map review, so the bundle member is the exact binary the build lane referenced.

currentnessAdjudication.finding: CR-289 is Rev. 10/24 and predates PL 2025, c. 513, which repealed § 2262-A(1) effective January 11, 2026. The form’s paragraph 1 still recites that the crime "is eligible for sealing under 15 M.R.S.A. § 2261(6) and § 2262-A" — a prerequisite the statute no longer imposes. The legal review names this in terms: "Release blocker for participant-facing accuracy: confirm whether the Judicial Branch has issued a revised CR-289."
currentnessAdjudication.whyThisBlocksAPacket: A production packet would put a participant’s signature under a recital of an eligibility requirement that no longer exists in law. That is a participant-facing accuracy defect on the face of the filing, not a rendering defect, and no amount of correct field placement cures it.

cr307Considered.findings: Encrypted, no XFA, 15 AcroForm fields, 1 page, created by Acrobat PDFMaker 26 for Word.
cr307Considered.rejectedAsSubstitute: CR-307 is Motion to Seal Conviction for Victims of Sex Trafficking or Sexual Exploitation — the survivor route, a different track from the former Class E engaging-in-prostitution route this job serves. The legal review treats them as separate tracks and directs screening every § 2262-A participant for the survivor route, but it never makes CR-307 the form for this one.

legalIntegrityDisposition: Deferred on currentness, not on availability. Tier 0 is technically satisfied and the implementation is ready to complete the moment the revision question closes either way.

participantTreatment.whyNoPacket: We will not prepare this motion while the official form is out of date. Form CR-289 is Rev. 10/24 and its first paragraph still says the crime must be "eligible for sealing under 15 M.R.S.A. § 2261(6) and § 2262-A" — a requirement the Legislature removed on 11 January 2026. Signing that would mean asserting a condition the law no longer imposes.
participantTreatment.whatTheParticipantIsTold: Maine law lets you seal a former Class E conviction for engaging in prostitution one year after you finish your sentence, and the court must grant it if you prove your case by the greater weight of the evidence. Once sealed, a later conviction does not unseal it and you have no duty to report anything. LegalEase is holding packet preparation until the Judicial Branch form matches the current statute.
participantTreatment.receivingAuthority: The clerk of the court where you were convicted — Superior Court, District Court or the Unified Criminal Docket, whichever handled your case.
participantTreatment.nextStep: Ask the clerk or courts.maine.gov for the current CR-289 and check whether a revision later than 10/24 has issued. Also ask about the sex-trafficking and sexual-exploitation survivor route on Form CR-307: it reaches any conviction and has no waiting period, so it may be the better route for you.
whatToGather: Your docket number and the court that handled the case
The date you finished every part of your sentence, including probation and fines
Any record showing the conviction was under former 17-A M.R.S. § 853-A
whatNotToFileOrRelyOn: Do not file a copy of CR-289 that still recites the § 2262-A(1) eligibility requirement without asking the clerk whether it is current
Do not use CR-218, the general sealing motion — it is a different route with a four-year wait and a lifetime self-reporting duty
Do not rely on any LegalEase-generated motion for this route; none exists
participantTreatment.briefcasePreservation: Your screening answers, your eligibility result and this handoff — including the court identified for you and the survivor-route question to ask — stay in your Briefcase, so the route resumes from what you already gave us once the form question closes.

blocker.exactMissingEvidence: Confirmation of whether the Maine Judicial Branch has issued a CR-289 revision after PL 2025, c. 513 (effective 2026-01-11), and the revised binary with its sha256 if one exists.
blocker.owner: source acquisition (operator or a lane with courts.maine.gov egress)
blocker.nextAction: Check the Maine Judicial Branch forms index for a CR-289 revision later than Rev. 10/24. If a revised form exists, supply it and lane E completes Tier 0 against it. If the Judicial Branch confirms Rev. 10/24 is still current, counsel records that the stale paragraph-1 recital is harmless for former § 853-A convictions — the legal review already reasons it is, because that offense sat outside Title 17-A chapter 11 — and lane E completes Tier 0 against the existing binary.

f2CorrectionRecord.whatWasWrong: Three decision-critical or participant-facing claims had no committed carrier: the whole deferral rested on PL 2025 c. 513 repealing § 2262-A(1), while the compiled profile mentions c. 513 only as creating the § 2262-B survivor route and never mentions § 2262-A; the participant was told the relief carries no continuing self-reporting duty; and the next step told them CR-307 has no waiting period. The document the adjudication cited was not in the repository at all.
f2CorrectionRecord.howItIsFixed: The adopted Maine legal design is pinned into this family as evidence with its sha256, and every claim now quotes it verbatim. Each quote is checked against the pinned bytes, so a claim cannot outlive its carrier.

en.whyNoPacket: We are not preparing this motion because the court’s form is older than the law it cites.
en.whatTheLawGives: You may seal the conviction one year after finishing your sentence, and the court must grant it if you prove your case by the greater weight of the evidence.
en.afterSealing: A later conviction does not unseal this record, and you have no duty to report anything afterwards.
en.whereToGo: File with the clerk of the court where you were convicted.
en.alsoAsk: Ask about the survivor route on Form CR-307. It reaches any conviction and has no waiting period.
en.briefcase: Your answers and this handoff stay in your Briefcase, so nothing is lost.
en.noCharge: You are not charged for this route and no packet credit is used.

es.whyNoPacket: No estamos preparando esta mocion porque el formulario del tribunal es anterior a la ley que cita.
es.whatTheLawGives: Puede sellar la condena un ano despues de cumplir su sentencia, y el tribunal debe concederlo si lo demuestra con la preponderancia de la prueba.
es.afterSealing: Una condena posterior no revoca el sellado de este registro, y usted no tiene ninguna obligacion de informarlo despues.
es.whereToGo: Presentela ante el secretario del tribunal donde fue condenado.
es.alsoAsk: Pregunte por la ruta para sobrevivientes en el formulario CR-307. Alcanza cualquier condena y no tiene periodo de espera.
es.briefcase: Sus respuestas y esta entrega permanecen en su Briefcase, para que no se pierda nada.
es.noCharge: No se le cobra por esta ruta y no se usa ningun credito de paquete.
